messages:
alex: Quick RFC follow-up — we need to decide how to synthesize a per-tenant SLA when the routing layer can pick between hosted, dedicated, and regional variants. TL;DR: do we compute a single merged latency/cost target upstream, or keep separate lane budgets and let runtime do the arbitration?

priya: Strong preference for explicit lanes. Merging hides signals and makes debugging fallback churn painful.

matt: Agree with priya but worried about explosion of constraints. Some tenants want 95th < 120ms, cost cap = $X, region pref = eu-west. If we keep separate lanes we need an efficient resolution step.

alex: Right. Two options sketch: 
1) Synthesized global SLA: upstream produces {latency_budget, cost_cap, region_affinity}. Runtime treats that as single objective score.
2) Lane-aware budgets: upstream emits per-lane budgets like {hosted:[80ms, $0.02], dedicated:[150ms, $0.01], region:...} and a tie-break policy.

sasha: Lane-aware seems better operationally. Example: customer sets strict latency; hosted satisfies but expensive. We can route to hosted with a short TTL then degrade. If only global signal exists, you lose the ability to step down gracefully.

matt: How about hybrid: synthesize a short primary budget + fallback lane set with soft penalties. That limits state while keeping graceful degrade.

priya: Implementation questions: where do we synthesize? control-plane policy service or policy sidecar? Centralized makes sense for uniformity, sidecars make fast local decisions and reduce RPCs.

alex: We ran sim tests last week. Centralized synth had better global cost smoothing but higher p95 variance on edge regions because of stale signals. Sidecar approach reduced regional p95 spikes but increased cost by 6% in heavy churn sims.

lia: infra-bot: load-test results uploaded: https://ci.redwood/tests/8342 (summary: central-synth cost -4% median, p95 +12% in ap-south under churn; sidecar cost +6%, p95 -9%)

sasha: Important: the policy API must expose explainability. Whatever we pick, ops need a quick trace: which lane, which penalty, what TTL. Otherwise SRE spends hours triaging.

matt: Agreed. Proposed minimal surface: 
```
SLA { tenant_id, requested_p95_ms, cost_cap_usd, region_pref }
RouteDecision { chosen_lane, score_breakdown: [latency_penalty, cost_penalty, affinity_bonus], ttl_seconds }
```

priya: +1. Also add `fallback_path` list for automated reroute troubleshooting.

alex: Edge case: mixed-model compatibility. Some dedicated GPUs don't support int4 kernels so effective model latency differs. We need lane capability tags and a compatibility step in synthesis. Otherwise global budgets are lie.

lia: infra-bot: added requirement: `lane_capabilities` to policy proto. See PR #412 on policy-service.

matt: One more tradeoff: preemption. If dedicated is a reserved pool, do we allow short preemptible requests to steal capacity when hosted is saturated? That complicates accounting.

sasha: My vote: allow preemption only for soft SLA tenants (flag on tenant). Requires chargeback tracking.

alex: Action items: 
- priya: draft policy proto for lane-aware budgets + fallback list (ETA: Thu)
- matt: add sim scenario for preemption and mixed-capability lanes (ETA: Fri)
- sasha: design tracing fields and sample UI wireframe for explainability (ETA: next Tue)
- infra-bot: link PRs into this thread when created

priya: noted. I'll include examples of synthesized output vs per-lane output for a few tenant profiles.

matt: If we can't converge on lane-aware within two weeks, fallback to hybrid synthesized primary + fallback set (Alex's option 2) so release isn't blocked.

alex: Cool. Thanks everyone. Marking this resolved for the RFC follow-up. We'll revisit after sims and proto drafts. :thumbsup:
